content: Benzonatate is a medication prescribed to alleviate coughing caused by conditions such as the common cold, bronchitis, pneumonia, or other lung infections. It belongs to a class of drugs known as antitussives, or cough suppressants. This medication works by suppressing the cough reflex in the lungs and airways. Benzonatate is available in two forms: liquid-filled capsules (also called perles) and standard capsules, both of which are taken orally. Typically, it is taken three times a day as needed. It is essential to follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully. If you have any questions or concerns, consult your doctor or pharmacist for clarification. Take the medication exactly as prescribed, without altering the dose or frequency. Swallow the capsules whole without chewing or sucking on them, as doing so may release the medication in your mouth, potentially causing numbness and an increased risk of choking. In some cases, benzonatate may be prescribed for purposes other than those listed. If you have questions about additional uses, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Before starting benzonatate, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to benzonatate, procaine (Novocain), tetracaine (Pontocaine), or any other medications. Additionally, provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, supplements, and herbal products you are currently taking. Notify your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking benzonatate. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness, so avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how it affects you. Alcohol can enhance the sedative effects of benzonatate, so it is advisable to avoid consuming alcohol while taking this medication. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, you may continue your normal diet while taking benzonatate. If you are taking benzonatate as needed, there is no strict dosing schedule. However, if your doctor has instructed you to take it regularly and you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Benzonatate may cause side effects. Minor side effects include upset stomach, constipation, drowsiness, headache, dizziness, nasal congestion, or a burning sensation in the eyes. If these symptoms persist or worsen, inform your doctor. Serious side effects are rare but require immediate medical attention. These include rash, hives, itching, difficulty breathing or swallowing, confusion, or hallucinations (seeing or hearing things that are not real). If you experience any unusual or severe side effects, contact your doctor promptly. Serious side effects can also be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store benzonatate in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly by consulting your pharmacist. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911 immediately. Symptoms of overdose may include restlessness, uncontrollable shaking, seizures, or loss of consciousness. Keep all scheduled appointments with your doctor while taking this medication. Do not share benzonatate with others, even if they have similar symptoms. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Benzonatate is sold under brand names such as Tessalon® Capsules and Tessalon® Perles.
